summary: Verified the unique_show_count popularity ranking feature end-to-end. Backend pytest 6/6 passed (new helper, /api/songs popularity sort, /api/songs unique_show_count field, public /api/musicians/{slug}/songs, /api/analytics/daily top_songs ranking, regression on request_count increment). Frontend Playwright covered Songs-tab Most Popular sort, Audience Most Popular sort, and Analytics Most Requested Songs (no badge, titles only, Top 10/20/50 dropdown).
critical_code_review_comments: VERIFIED: backend helper get_unique_show_counts (server.py L3836-3866) uses a single $match ($ne archived, song_id $in list) + $group $addToSet show_id + $project $size aggregation. Songs with no matching requests are correctly omitted (callers default to 0).

VERIFIED: GET /api/songs (server.py L3869-3955) attaches unique_show_count to every Song and, when sort_by=popularity, sorts in-memory by unique_show_count desc AFTER attaching the field. Empirical proof from live DB: Test Song (usc=7, request_count=86) ranks #1, Test Song 1 (usc=6, request_count=10) ranks #2 — confirming raw request_count is no longer the primary key.
VERIFIED: Public GET /api/musicians/{slug}/songs (server.py L4349-4368) attaches unique_show_count without disturbing request_count or requests_this_show.

VERIFIED: GET /api/analytics/daily top_songs (server.py L4998-5052) ranks by len(set(show_id)) per song_id, limited to 50 items (was 10) to support the Top 50 UI option. count field in payload equals the unique-show count.
VERIFIED: Song Pydantic model (server.py L229) declares unique_show_count: int = 0 as a transient (response-only) field — not persisted to DB.
VERIFIED: Frontend applySorting (App.js L2523-2524) and applyAudienceSorting (App.js L10440-10441) both sort by (b.unique_show_count || 0) - (a.unique_show_count || 0).

VERIFIED: Analytics Most Requested Songs (App.js L8431-8445) container has data-testid='most-requested-songs-list', renders only

{item.song}

, no badge / no .bg-purple-600 chip. Top 10/20/50 dropdown still functional.

VERIFIED regression: POST /api/requests still increments request_count and requests_this_show; new test exercises a fresh song through one show and asserts request_count>=1, requests_this_show>=1, unique_show_count==1.

MINOR (pre-existing, intentional per spec): $addToSet of show_id will treat null/None as a distinct value. If a song has both null-show_id and one real show_id, unique_show_count would be 2. Per problem statement this is intentional, but worth a future ticket if product wants to ignore null show_ids.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (Songs sort, Audience sort, Analytics rendering, Top 10/20/50)

seed_data_creation: Created 2 TEST_ songs (TEST_UniqueShowSong_<hex>, TEST_RegSong_<hex>) and ephemeral shows TEST_Show_<hex>/TEST_RegShow_<hex>. Posted 4 requests against TEST_UniqueShowSong across two distinct shows to validate distinct-show counting (yielding unique_show_count==2). Teardown archives the seeded requests and stops the shows; song/profile rows remain clearly TEST_ prefixed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run the regression with `REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=$(grep REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL /app/frontend/.env | cut -d= -f2) python -m pytest backend/tests/test_unique_show_count_popularity.py -v`. The test file seeds its own data (TEST_-prefixed) so it can run repeatedly. Frontend testid contract: most-requested-songs-list (Analytics), Songs-tab sort select has option value 'popularity', audience sort select has option value 'most-popular'. Public musician slug URL is /musician/test (not /m/test). For login automation, use input[type=email] / input[type=password] on the root page; there is no /login route. Use page.evaluate fetch with localStorage.getItem('token') to make authenticated requests from the browser context (avoids Cloudflare 1010 bot block on direct urllib).
